item.title: Using Pageweft
item.description:
See a completed result

Open Pageweft or explore the original PDF/Markdown/ZIP example linked from its website and the portfolio. Viewing the completed example does not run a GPU conversion.

Inspect before processing

Upload a PDF you have permission to process. Each file can be at most 64 MiB and 1,000 PDF pages; up to five files can be inspected, with each conversion confirmed separately. Choose the original PDF page numbers or ranges and review the text-layer inspection and quote.

item.title: Building Pageweft: extraction to a hosted workbench
item.description:
1. Establish actual extraction

The initial requirement was private PDF-to-Markdown preparation using MinerU on the owner’s Modal account. The design moved from customer-provided Modal credentials to owner-hosted processing; customers do not provide cloud tokens. MinerU 2.7.6 runs in a cloud GPU image and retains original engine output. The laptop’s 2 GB GPU is not required.

A bounded one-page public trial was verified before describing full-book processing. The initial deployed web startup failed because modal_fn.py was missing from its uploaded source. Explicit inclusion fixed the image, followed by a fresh deployment and public workflow checks. Original verification record .

item.title: Technical overview
item.description:
Hosted PDF workflow

Pageweft runs a Python/FastAPI web interface and serialized SQLite ledger on Modal behind Cloudflare. Inspect authorized PDFs up to 64 MiB / 1,000 pages, choose original page ranges and review the extraction plan/quote. Automatic routing uses text extraction or pinned MinerU OCR; forced OCR and explicit CPU text-only routes remain separate. Text-only does not reconstruct images or full layout.

Bounded sections preserve completed output through partial failures. Review against source pages, retain engine versions separately from corrections, and export single/per-page/group/bookmark Markdown with relative media and hashed provenance. Plain Markdown, Obsidian and LLM-oriented presets are formatting choices, not generated summaries or accuracy guarantees.

item.title: Conversion product design
item.description:
Implementation update

The approved core features are now implemented: full-book/range inspection (bounded at 64 MiB/1,000 pages), batch inspection, quotes, bounded section processing, selective retries/force OCR, source-linked review, corrections/history, portable outputs and prepaid-credit accounting. Read BOOK-RELEASE.md for tested evidence and limits. Earlier candidate language below describes the design rationale. Actual merchant activation and comparative difficult-document fidelity remain unverified; these features do not certify every source symbol.

Pageweft: conversion utility

User clarification, 14 October 2026: PDF-to-Markdown for serious work with books, including Linguavell preparation. Users control the downstream reading/LLM workflow. No study platform, AI chat, automatically generated teaching materials or decorative feature expansion.

item.title: Dependencies and licensing
item.description:
19 October: exact current web/MinerU Python package versions, declared license metadata and wheel license-file hashes are now recorded in image inventory . This replaces the older “no inventory” statement only for the Python distribution layer; bundled native/system libraries, complete model terms and compatibility still require the stated review. No licensing conclusion is inferred from metadata.

Third-party source notes

Verified 14 October 2026. The extraction worker installs the official PyPI release mineru[pipeline]==2.7.6 and invokes its CLI without patching it. Official source release: mineru-2.7.6-released , commit e31c0ec34da89f6d7db78866ffec13eb0aaa3a3c. That release’s LICENSE.md is GNU Affero General Public License version 3. Current master licensing must not be substituted for the pinned release’s terms.

item.title: Owner operations
item.description:
Current public operating boundary

Pageweft runs behind its public Cloudflare gateway on Modal. Email-first signup, verification and mailed resets for verified addresses are deployed alongside private-key recovery. Accounts and balances are product-specific. Dedicated Google/GitHub registration and genuine consent remain unaccepted; checkout is closed.

Admission and privacy

Live free processing checks visitor eligibility and private shared availability before dispatch. An unavailable or unverifiable admission check refuses new processing with Currently unavailable. Please try again later. Completed examples remain open. Signing in does not reset sample eligibility.

item.title: Launch readiness register
item.description:
What visitors can use

The completed PDF example, public guide, private email account/recovery flow and bounded processing interface are deployed. Live sample availability is checked privately and may temporarily close; an example remains useful without another processing job.

What is still gated

Paid processing packs remain closed. App-domain approval is owner-reported; actual seller/payout readiness and genuine payment/refund/payout acceptance still require their own evidence. Do not infer merchant readiness from a successful processing demo or mocked payment tests.

item.title: Book conversion release
item.description:
Original record: Book conversion release — 14 October 2026.

Implemented in the hosted Pageweft application; supersedes the one-page-only product and $1/month access proposal. Amir delegated a better pricing model and approved the conversion utility improvements. The public free sample remains one selected page, but inspection accepts books and paid jobs use separately funded credits.

Features and implementation

Capability Implementation
Books / ranges / batch inspection Up to five PDFs, each <=64 MiB and 1,000 source PDF pages; strict PDF validation and page-range parser; retained inspected PDFs can be resumed. Each conversion is separately confirmed.
Preview and price before extraction Source page count, selected pages and text-layer samples are inspected without GPU work; fixed tariff quote must match the confirmation.
Automatic / force OCR / cheaper text-only Pinned unmodified MinerU 2.7.6 uses its documented mode/language options; pypdf text-only worker uses no GPU and explicitly excludes OCR, image extraction and layout reconstruction.
Bounded sections / partial recovery Selected pages split into groups of 20; at most two GPU workers. Successful sections survive failures; explicit retries select missing or chosen original pages and can force OCR. Duplicate requests cannot reserve or dispatch twice.
Traceability / fidelity review Original page indices are mapped from the subset PDF back to the full source. Renderer preserves recognized headings, equations, HTML tables, captions, footnotes and images. Unhandled blocks, unmapped content, empty/short output, missing images and replacement glyphs are reported. Untouched engine output is retained separately; flags do not certify correctness.
Corrections / history Plain Markdown editor with original-PDF page link, optimistic edit versions and saved history. Reprocessing retains user corrections. Engine text can be loaded explicitly into the editor draft.
Portable outputs Single Markdown, individual pages, bounded page groups, or sections based on original PDF bookmarks. Local image paths, source hash, unavailable-page list, raw section extraction and review metadata. Source PDF inclusion is optional.
Cancel / discard / delete / expiry Queued work releases reserved allowance. A running cancelled section may finish and be charged. Job deletion removes edits/output and releases an unshared source. Unused inspected sources can be discarded. Hourly cleanup removes 48-hour-expired files; balances/recovery persist separately.
Account / purchase recovery Encrypted Secure/HttpOnly session; high-entropy recovery key stored only as keyed hash. One-time purchase keys can restore the owning account. No customer Modal credentials.
Payments / refunds Separate one-time pack integration verifies scoped provider orders and signed events; duplicate orders grant once, full/partial refunds revoke pack credits. Atomic reserve/settle/release accounting in integer 1/10,000 USD units. Public test-mode grants disabled. Live seller configuration remains absent.

The active HTTP factory is web/studio.py. web/main.py and web/billing.py preserve the retired interface/verifier for regression/compatibility work; they are not the public paid implementation. Books use /ledger/books.sqlite, separate from the original /ledger/state.sqlite. Each is owned by one serialized function. Do not run a second Modal app with a separate book_store function on the same volume. Owner verification scripts invoke deployed functions instead.

item.title: Paddle integration evidence

item.title: Extraction verification record
item.description:
Original record: Hosted trial evidence — 14 October 2026.

Scope: owner-hosted PDF-to-Markdown trial, not live commerce, academic-document fidelity certification or full-book acceptance.

  • Automated: .venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests -v — 22 passed. Includes real SQLite persistence and 30 concurrent quota attempts; PDF/session/ownership/archive checks; fake CLI and mocked payment-provider boundaries explicitly remain simulated.
  • Static: node --check static/app.js, Git whitespace check passed after removing one trailing space.
  • Real private compute: original one-page PDF processed on A10G by pinned MinerU 2.7.6; readable expected text, original PDF, source mapping and review report in a 2,295-byte ZIP. No copyrighted book was submitted for this probe.
  • Real hosted HTTP: /health and /api/session returned 200, billing_enabled=false, old /upload returned 404. Upload → job polling → completed ZIP download passed. Duplicate request returned the same job. Separate session received 404 for both status and download.
  • Browser: Playwright 1.63.0 with system Chromium and chromiumSandbox=true, widths 320/390/768/1440. No horizontal overflow or page errors. Oversize file rejected in browser; invalid PDF rejected by real HTTP service without dispatch; retry reenabled; privacy disclosure keyboard action worked. Phone/desktop screenshots inspected. No physical iPhone or Safari certification.
  • Deployment: .venv/bin/python -m modal deploy app.py succeeded; public URL https://m-amir-gomaa--mineru-pdf-extractor-web-app.modal.run . First startup failed due to missing modal_fn.py; explicit inclusion fixed it and checks above were run after redeployment.

Private artifacts live in ignored artifacts/: verification.pdf, verification-result.zip, public-verification-result.zip, public-verification.json, browser-verification.json and browser screenshots. No session cookies, CSRF values or provider credentials are in this evidence. One bounded real public trial was consumed; unit and browser-invalid-input checks did not submit additional GPU work.

item.title: Accessibility review — 16 October
item.description:
Original record: Retained-document panel accessibility — 16 October 2026.

The inspected-PDF list had an aria-label on an otherwise generic div. Its explicit region role now gives that existing label valid semantics. No job, file, quote, credit, payment or storage behavior changes.

All 78 existing tests passed. The existing Modal deployment succeeded in 4.110 seconds at its unchanged hostname. Runtime secrets, volumes, balances and disabled billing were preserved; no extraction, funded fixture or real purchase was run. Hosted narrow/desktop and automated WCAG checks are recorded in the supporting portfolio release milestone. Unrelated bytecode/book-workflow changes remain outside this commit.

item.title: Custom domain and account access
item.description:
Public address: https://pageweft.amirgomaa.com/ . A fixed-origin Cloudflare Workers Free gateway connects to the preserved Modal endpoint; Modal still runs the app and processing. No Team upgrade or live payment activation was made. The shared reproducible gateway source/config/tests and rollout guide are in the workspace at freelance/workflow/cloudflare-edge/.

Session/payment secrets, volumes, existing balances and processing limits remain unchanged. A separate pageweft-edge Modal secret authenticates time-bounded client-IP assertions from this Worker for rate quotas. Direct Modal requests retain the existing last-proxy-hop fallback. The web boundary still verifies CSRF tokens; the gateway rejects unsafe cross-origin requests before mapping its own trusted Origin to the upstream origin. Uploads/responses stream, cache mode is explicitly no-store, and cookies stay host-only Secure/HttpOnly. Initial live verification caught and corrected a TTL-zero cache override that stripped cookies; do not reintroduce cf.cacheTtl: 0 as a cache-disable switch.

item.title: Source workflow and diagnostics release
item.description:
Original record: Source workflow and diagnostics — 18 October 2026.

Extraction lineage follow-through — 19 October 2026

Reprocessing now exposes the original extractor versions alongside the preserved user correction. The history reader returns the first and 19 most recent versions when there are more than 20, limiting loaded sections and returned text. Loading or selecting a version never saves it; copying it into the editor asks before discarding an unsaved draft. Explicit Save retains the existing conflict check and correction history. Expired/deleted or another owner’s conversions cannot be read. A failed retry leaves the earlier successful extraction available.

item.title: Quality and cost measurement
item.description:
Offline scoring

scripts/score_quality.py compares human-prepared comparable text and observed measurements. It never uploads files, calls a model, spends credits or silently changes app limits. It reports exact character/word edit rates, not factual correctness or a calibrated confidence badge. Case, punctuation, numeric values, diacritics and technical symbols remain significant; only Unicode NFC and CRLF representation normalize. Whitespace splits word tokens, so CER is generally the more useful measure for languages without space-delimited words.

item.title: Declared image package inventory
item.description:
Actual ephemeral CPU inspection of the current deployment package image definitions. Full wheel metadata and license-file hashes ; SHA256 4b3bbd7a425c300a9563cfe4a147b0bb1d3e6e49d29a119c7ff75d216d0d1161. No GPU, model download, customer volume or secret was used. This records installed Python distributions, not a legal compatibility approval. Bundled native/system libraries and model weights need separate review; exact previously observed model revisions and upstream terms are in third-party source notes .

Reproduce using PYTHONPATH=. .venv_modal_new/bin/python -m modal run scripts/dependency_inventory_modal.py --output NEW_PRIVATE_JSON. Choose an exclusive output; no current app/volume/secret is replaced. An ephemeral owner app stops after the metadata read. Two initial attempts exposed duplicate function tags and a missing source module with include_source=False; the final implementation uses distinct functions in the image-contained web module. These failed reads produced no claimed inventory.

item.title: Verified email and recovery
item.description:
Create and recover an account

Open Account to sign in with an existing passphrase. New email signup requests a link; explicitly choosing a passphrase on its confirmation form creates the credential. Opening a link alone does not create it. Existing unverified accounts can verify their address from their owned, recently authenticated workspace. Equal addresses never merge workspaces.

Verified addresses can request mailed resets. Completion revokes previous sessions and invalidates old recovery keys. Links expire after thirty minutes and work once; opening/previewing does not consume them. A separate saved key is optional when verified email recovery is available. Keep any key private.

item.title: From sources to connected notes
item.description:
Pageweft converts PDF pages to Markdown. Sonaweft transcribes recordings. Noteweld keeps editable notes, links, source material and portable vaults.

  1. Use Pageweft or Sonaweft, review the original against the result, and save any corrections.
  2. Download a fresh complete ZIP bundle from that application’s workspace.
  3. In Noteweld, open Source bundles, choose Pageweft or Sonaweft export, and validate the ZIP.
  4. Review its contents, confirm permission to retain them, and import. Notes and their original archive commit together. The original extraction, corrections and optional AI notes keep separate labels.
  5. Edit and link the imported notes. Download the original bundle or export a portable vault when needed.

The current Noteweld preview accepts an archive up to 4 MiB and 250 notes, subject to remaining account capacity. Pageweft can export fewer pages and omit the source PDF. A smaller recording gives a smaller Sonaweft bundle. Keep your own originals; a bundle includes source media only when the exporter includes it.
